summary: Yedinka Airport (EDN) is a small regional airport serving the remote settlement of Yedinka in Primorsky Krai, in the Russian Far East. Located near the coast of the Sea of Japan, it primarily supports local transportation needs in this sparsely populated and geographically isolated region. The airport plays a vital role in connecting the community to larger regional centers, given the limited road infrastructure in the surrounding area.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft typically use Yedinka Airport?
A: The airport primarily handles small regional aircraft suitable for short-haul flights, given its modest infrastructure and runway.

Q: Are there regular commercial flights to Yedinka?
A: Scheduled service is limited and infrequent, as the airport mainly serves local and charter needs rather than regular commercial routes.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small airport, facilities are minimal, typically including a basic terminal building and limited passenger amenities.

Q: Is Yedinka Airport accessible year-round?
A: Operations can be affected by weather conditions, particularly during the harsh winter months common in the Russian Far East.
transport_tips: Getting to Yedinka Airport requires planning, as the area is remote with limited road access. Travelers typically rely on regional flights from Khabarovsk or Vladivostok to reach the area. Local transport options to and from the airport are minimal, so arranging ground transportation in advance is highly recommended.
local_tip: Pack layers regardless of the season — the coastal Far East climate can shift quickly between chilly sea winds and warmer inland conditions, even in summer.
